subprocess_flow.description: Examine the AI System Architecture Design Document and Infrastructure as Code (IaC) templates to verify structural compliance with MoJ Secure by Design standards and NIST SP 800-53 controls. The cyber security engineering team evaluates network topologies, container configurations, and orchestration pipelines to confirm strict OFFICIAL-SENSITIVE boundary controls.
subprocess_flow.responsible_party: Chief Information Security Officer (CISO) & Cyber Security Team
subprocess_flow.purpose: Verify foundational cloud and on-premises infrastructure templates comply with Ministry of Justice security baselines.
subprocess_flow.scope: IaC repositories (Terraform/CloudFormation), network routing topologies, and system architecture blueprints.
subprocess_flow.process_owner: MoJ Chief Enterprise Architect & Head of Data Governance
triggers: Completion of data quality validation and submission of system architecture documentation
end_conditions: Infrastructure code baseline review approved with zero unmitigated security architectural non-conformances

step_risks_and_controls.risk: Misconfigured infrastructure allowing unauthorized public access to sensitive justice environments
step_risks_and_controls.control: Automated static analysis of IaC templates using checkov and tfsec against MoJ Secure by Design rulesets

change_management.change_request_process: Architectural deviations submitted to CISO Technical Review Panel via ServiceNow RFC
change_management.versioning_rules: IaC repositories version-controlled with semantic git tags

improvement_inputs: MoJ Secure by Design pattern updates

subprocess_flow.substep_name: Perform Threat Modeling and Attack Surface Analysis
subprocess_flow.description: Construct an AI threat model using STRIDE and NIST AI RMF GOVERN/PROTECT frameworks based on data flow diagrams and the approved architecture. This assessment pinpoints AI-specific attack vectors including prompt injection, model inversion, training data extraction, and adversarial inputs targeting court or offender data stores.
subprocess_flow.responsible_party: Chief Information Security Officer (CISO) & Cyber Security Team
subprocess_flow.purpose: Identify adversarial attack vectors and AI-specific vulnerabilities across inference endpoints, pipelines, and data storage.
subprocess_flow.scope: Data ingestion feeds, API interfaces, training pipelines, model registries, and runtime inference environments.
subprocess_flow.process_owner: MoJ Chief Enterprise Architect & Head of Data Governance
triggers: Completion of Review Architecture and Infrastructure Code
end_conditions: Threat model signed off and mitigation tasks cataloged in project backlog

step_risks_and_controls.risk: Unidentified AI-specific attack vectors leading to model poisoning or extraction
step_risks_and_controls.control: Mandatory AI threat modeling workshop following OWASP AI Top 10 and NIST AI RMF guidelines

governance_requirements: NIST AI RMF - GOVERN & PROTECT Functions

change_management.change_request_process: Threat model revisions tracked alongside project sprint changes
change_management.versioning_rules: Threat models versioned in git repository as markdown/draw.io artifacts

improvement_inputs: UK AI Safety Institute vulnerability feeds

subprocess_flow.description: Conduct deep technical inspection of cryptographic implementations and enclave perimeter isolation controls. The security team verifies KMS envelope encryption using customer-managed keys (CMK), mTLS across microservices, and network micro-segmentation preventing lateral traversal between general MoJ networks and sensitive offender record enclaves.
subprocess_flow.responsible_party: Chief Information Security Officer (CISO) & Cyber Security Team
subprocess_flow.purpose: Ensure cryptographic protection at rest and in transit aligns with HMG OFFICIAL-SENSITIVE handling rules.
subprocess_flow.scope: KMS key hierarchies, TLS configurations, VPC peering/PrivateLink connections, and data store encryption configs.
subprocess_flow.process_owner: MoJ Chief Enterprise Architect & Head of Data Governance
triggers: Completion of Perform Threat Modeling and Attack Surface Analysis
end_conditions: Cryptographic configurations and enclave boundaries validated with formal passing test audit logs

step_risks_and_controls.risk: Data exfiltration via unencrypted inter-service communication or weak key storage
step_risks_and_controls.control: Enforcement of FIPS 140-3 validated KMS modules, mandatory TLS 1.3, and strict VPC service perimeter controls

change_management.change_request_process: KMS policy or network boundary adjustments require CISO Security Architecture sign-off
change_management.versioning_rules: Key policies and security group definitions managed under git version control

improvement_inputs: VPC flow logs and intrusion detection anomaly reports

subprocess_flow.description: Execute targeted penetration testing and red-teaming exercises against the containerized AI pipelines, inference APIs, and data access endpoints. Testing covers standard web application vulnerabilities as well as adversarial model evasion, evasion payload injection, and privilege escalation within the secure cloud enclave.
subprocess_flow.responsible_party: Chief Information Security Officer (CISO) & Cyber Security Team
subprocess_flow.purpose: Discover exploitable weaknesses in live test environments before staging production deployment.
subprocess_flow.scope: Runtime AI container endpoints, orchestration control planes, authentication gateways, and data stores.
subprocess_flow.process_owner: MoJ Chief Enterprise Architect & Head of Data Governance
triggers: Completion of Validate Encryption and Enclave Boundaries
end_conditions: Zero open critical or high severity vulnerabilities verified and documented in penetration testing summary

step_risks_and_controls.risk: Unresolved zero-day or high-risk vulnerabilities present in runtime AI container dependencies
step_risks_and_controls.control: Dynamic application security testing (DAST), container image scanning, and third-party penetration testing

governance_requirements: NIST SP 800-115 Technical Guide to Information Security Testing and Assessment

change_management.change_request_process: Vulnerability remediation commits tracked in Jira and verified via re-test scans
change_management.versioning_rules: Penetration test findings tracked under MoJ Defect Management System with build IDs

improvement_inputs: Mean time to remediate (MTTR) critical findings

subprocess_flow.description: Collate findings from the threat model, encryption verification, and penetration test summary into a consolidated MoJ Secure by Design AI Compliance Review dossier. The CISO and Cyber Security Team formally review the artifacts against acceptance criteria and issue the formal Security Sign-off Certificate.
subprocess_flow.responsible_party: Chief Information Security Officer (CISO) & Cyber Security Team
subprocess_flow.purpose: Provide formal, auditable security certification permitting the AI solution to advance to ethical and governance review stages.
subprocess_flow.scope: Consolidated security dossier, residual risk registers, and formal security certification records.
subprocess_flow.process_owner: MoJ Chief Enterprise Architect & Head of Data Governance
triggers: Successful remediation of all penetration testing findings and completion of testing summary
end_conditions: Issuance of signed MoJ Security Sign-off Certificate and registration in central governance repository
